newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portucel optimistic on pulp sector.
newsitem.headline: Portucel optimistic on pulp sector.

text.p: The pulp and paper sector has good prospects for growth over the next 18 months with demand and supply in balance, the chairman of Portucel Industrial said on Tuesday.
"Demand and supply will be balanced both this year and next and therefore sales should be good," Jorge Godinho told Reuters.
"There is optimism about the immediate outlook for the end of 1997 and the beginning of 1998", he added without giving any figures.
State-controlled Portucel Industrial-Empresa Produtora de Celulose is due to present its first half results on July 31.
Godinho said that the decision of two big Indonesian producers to suspend projects to build new plants was good news for the industry.
"The cancellation, or at least the postponement, of these two projects...will bring greater equilibrium to the market in the short and medium term," he said.
Astra International and Indah Kiat announced recently that they were cancelling and suspending, respectively, plans for new pulp facilities in Indonesia.
"They (the Indonesians) have in fact cheaper wood but building new plants from scratch costs a lot of money and they were not ready to take it (the risk) on," he added.
Portucel shares were gaining three escudos at 1,413 escudos on Tuesday.
